name: Smiling Face with Tear
baseMeaning: A face smiling with a single tear.
tldr: 🥲 shows you are touched by good news, kindness, or a bittersweet moment, with the smile still intact.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🥲 marks a happy, tender, or bittersweet reaction to something that felt bigger than an ordinary smile could express.
Used carefully, 🥲 can acknowledge real sadness while showing that the sender is still trying to smile through it.
In a close romantic exchange, 🥲 can show that a thoughtful gesture or sweet news genuinely moved the sender.
🥲 can congratulate someone on a personal or professional win without turning the reaction into a boast or a joke.

platformNotes.note: 🥲 often appears as a quick closing mark after a sincere sentence in personal conversations. The nearby words usually tell you whether it means happiness, gratitude, or sadness.
In comments and direct messages, 🥲 works as a compact reaction to touching news or a heartfelt post. On a public comment, the emotion may be broader than the sender’s personal story.
People commonly use 🥲 on captions or replies when a video is unexpectedly sweet or emotionally bittersweet. The emoji alone may suggest that something affected them more than they can explain.
🥲 can close a family or friend message after good news, a milestone, or a goodbye. Because the emoji carries both warmth and a tear, its meaning depends heavily on the sentence around it.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z users often treat 🥲 as a concise way to say “this really moved me.” It can carry happiness, tenderness, and sadness at the same time without a longer explanation.
Millennials commonly use 🥲 around personal milestones, meaningful goodbyes, and thoughtful acts from friends or partners. It often sounds affectionate and emotionally sincere.

Gen X users may still recognize 🥲 as a moved reaction, especially when the message names the good news or loss. In mixed-age conversations, clear words help prevent a tear emoji from sounding too casual.

warnings.title: Too small for real grief
warnings.description: At a serious loss, bereavement, or betrayal, 🥲 can sound as though the sender is performing an emotional reaction rather than meeting the moment. Use 😢 or 😭 and name what happened instead.

warnings.title: Reading it as plain happiness
warnings.description: 🥲 is not simply a cheerful smile; the tear marks a complicated feeling. If the sender wants to celebrate without sadness or emotional strain, a simpler emoji may fit better.

seoTitle: 🥲 Smiling Face with Tear Emoji Meaning
seoDescription: What does 🥲 mean? It shows you are touched, moved, or emotionally full after good news, kindness, an accomplishment, or a bittersweet moment.

longForm.overview:
🥲 is a face with a small smile and one tear, and that combination matters. It is usually sent when something has moved the sender: good news, a thoughtful gesture, a personal achievement, or a moment that is happy and sad at once. The smile says there is warmth in the moment; the tear says it still has emotional weight.

It differs from its nearby crying emojis by size and intent. 😢 is the straightforward “I am sad with you” choice, while 😭 is the louder, overwhelmed cry. 🥺 is closer to “please” or “trying not to cry.” 🥲 does the more specific job of expressing being touched. That makes it natural after “I got the job 🥲” or “that is so sweet 🥲,” but too small for a friend’s serious loss. The common mistake is treating the smile as the only message, or the tear as proof of deep sadness. Usually, both are part of what the sender feels.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🥲 tends to arrive as a bare reaction after someone shares good news, a vulnerable post, a thoughtful surprise, or a bittersweet scene from a show. “the finale broke me 🥲” is a familiar shape: the sender wants to say that the ending was sad, beautiful, and worth the reaction all at once.

It also works at the end of a goodbye or a personal milestone. “last day at the office 🥲” acknowledges a real loss while showing that the sender is managing it with a smile. A single 🥲 can close a message after a kind act, a job offer, or an accomplishment that took effort. The sender is usually trying to say, “This means something to me,” not simply “I am crying.”
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not use 🥲 for a major bereavement, a painful breakup, a serious betrayal, or another moment that needs direct sympathy. In those situations it can seem too small, as though the sender is asking the other person to soften the loss. The better choice is usually 😢 or 😭 with a sentence that says what happened.

Be careful with professional and mixed-age settings too. A heart emoji can look overly sentimental when the message is supposed to remain straightforward, and a tear may make a workplace congratulation sound unexpectedly personal. If the emotion is simple happiness, use a smile or celebration emoji. If it is actual sadness, use 😢. 🥲 works best when the moment is genuinely moving but not larger than the tear can hold.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🥲, match the feeling rather than repeating the emoji mechanically. After “I got the job 🥲,” congratulate them directly: “I’m so happy for you, you earned this.” After a kind gesture, “that really was thoughtful of you” or “you made my day” confirms that you understood the tenderness.

You can also send 🥲 back when you feel the same way, but words often make the reply more personal. If the emoji appears under your own news, do not assume it means the sender is jealous or upset; it often simply marks the moment as meaningful. If you are unsure, ask whether they mean “I’m happy for you” or “I’m a little sad about this.” A short clarification can preserve the warmth without making the exchange heavier.

faqs.question: What does 🥲 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: Usually it means he is moved by what you shared, whether that is good news, a thoughtful gesture, or an emotional moment. It is not automatically romantic, though it can be affectionate in a dating thread.

faqs.question: Is 🥲 flirty?
faqs.answer: 🥲 can appear in flirtatious messages because it communicates tenderness and being emotionally affected. The meaning comes from the relationship and surrounding words, not from the emoji alone.

faqs.question: What does 🥲 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🥲 is often used for a video that is sweet, touching, unexpectedly sad, or beautifully bittersweet. It signals that the content affected the sender more than an ordinary reaction would show.

faqs.question: Should I use 🥲 or 😭 for bad news?
faqs.answer: Use 🥲 for sadness mixed with a smile, such as a meaningful goodbye or a bittersweet ending. Use 😭 when the sender is overwhelmed, and use 😢 for ordinary sadness or sympathy.

conversationExamples.message: you remembered that i had that awful day 🥲
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is touched by a thoughtful gesture and may also be relieved or nostalgic. Respond with warm appreciation, such as “I really needed that yesterday,” rather than treating it as a joke.
This is a personal win with some history behind it, so 🥲 acknowledges both the happiness and how hard the sender worked. Congratulate them and mention the effort if you know it.

conversationExamples.message: the presentation landed better than i expected 🥲
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is relieved, proud, and still feeling the pressure of the event. An appreciative “That’s great, you earned the nerves” suits the moment better than a joke.

conversationExamples.message: today was grandma’s last day at home 🥲
conversationExamples.interpretation: The smile and tear show a bittersweet goodbye, but the subject is serious grief. Acknowledge the family directly and offer comfort; do not make the emoji the main reassurance.

conversationExamples.message: that ending was beautiful but i’m still crying 🥲
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is reacting to a bittersweet fictional moment, probably a finale or powerful scene. Join the emotion with “It got me right in the feelings” or describe the part that hit hardest.
